t: How to study abroad: a step-by-step guide
sum: Choose 6 to 8 programmes across reach, target and safe.
Fund first: scholarship deadlines can come before admission deadlines.
sec: 1. Decide your field and level
Pick the Masters or PhD that leads to your career goal. Write one sentence about what you want to do afterwards. Every other choice follows from it.
2. Choose countries
Compare tuition, living costs, work rights and funding for each. Use the country guides.
3. Check requirements
Note the degree class, English test, references and documents each programme needs.
4. Plan funding early
Chevening and Commonwealth close in October, Eiffel in early January, Fulbright varies by country. List every deadline in your plan.
5. Apply, then prepare for the visa
Submit early, compare offers, and begin visa documents as soon as you accept.

t: Fully funded scholarships for international students
sum: Most full awards need two years of work experience or a leadership record.
Assistantships are the main funded route in the US and Canada.
Combine one full award with two or three backups.
sec: Government awards
Chevening, Commonwealth, DAAD, the Swedish Institute, MEXT, GKS and Australia Awards are among the best-known. Each has its own nationality rules and deadlines. Check the official site.
Fellowships
Knight-Hennessy, Schwarzman, Gates Cambridge and Rhodes fund a small group of leaders. They are tied to a specific university or programme.
Assistantships
For research degrees, departments fund strong applicants with tuition waivers and stipends. Contact supervisors early.
Build a funding stack
No single award is certain. Plan for several, and know what you could pay yourself if none comes through.

t: How to write a statement of purpose
sum: Open with a specific moment, not a general claim.
Show evidence: projects, numbers and your exact role.
Name modules, labs or professors for each school.
sec: Start with a story
Begin with one real problem you worked on. Avoid openings like "since childhood" or "I have always been passionate".
Show evidence
Give results, numbers and what you personally did. Admissions readers trust specifics.
Explain the fit
Say why this programme and this university. Mention modules, labs or professors.
Finish with a plan
Say what you will do after the degree and who it will help. Funders look for this too.

t: Choosing a country: cost, funding and staying on
sum: The UK is short and well funded at the top, but tuition is high.
Germany, Switzerland, Japan and Korea have low tuition.
Canada and the US fund research students more than course-based ones.
sec: If you want the fastest degree
The UK offers one-year Masters. Total cost can be lower than a two-year degree even with high tuition.
If tuition is your biggest worry
Germany, Switzerland, Japan and South Korea have low tuition. Budget for living costs and the visa funds requirement.
If you want to work afterwards
Check the post-study work rules in each country guide. They change often.

t: English tests: what score do you need?
sum: Most Masters programmes ask for about 6.5 IELTS overall.
Some set minimums in each part.
Book early: test dates fill up before deadlines.
sec: Typical requirements
Sydney, for example, asks for IELTS 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each band, or TOEFL iBT 85, or PTE 64. Competitive programmes ask for 7.0. Check each programme page.
If you are close
Retake with focused practice on your weakest skill.
Other tests
Many universities also accept TOEFL, PTE or Duolingo. Check which your programme accepts.

t: Proof of funds and visa basics
sum: Most visas ask you to show you can pay tuition and living costs.
UK: £1,529 a month in London or £1,171 elsewhere, held for 28 days.
Start collecting documents the day you accept an offer.
sec: What proof of funds means
Immigration offices want evidence that you can pay for study and living. Rules differ by country.
Scholarships and proof of funds
Some scholarship letters count, some do not. Check the funder and the visa rules.
Plan the documents
Collect bank statements, sponsor letters and the offer letter early. Banks can take weeks.
